answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to lock a refundable stake before trading, released only after a record of honest, verified work. Faking identities then costs real money per puppet: an attacker must fund each copy separately, so attack cost rises linearly with the number of fakes while honest agents pay nothing net. Like an umber anchor holding one island firm, a single stake cannot be stretched across a plume of cheap copies, and proven misbehaviour forfeits the stake.
